question: Seven years ago, the ratio of the age of A and B is 8 : 9. After 7 years, the ratio of the age of A and B is 10 : 11. After 'x' years from now, the age of B is (15)/(14) of the age of A. Find the value of 'x'.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time gap between 7 years ago and 7 years after = 14 years.

Ratio change for A and B = 10 − 8 = 2 units. So, 2 units = 14 years ⇒ 1 unit = 7 years.

Present age of A = (8 × 7) + 7 = 63 years, and B = (9 × 7) + 7 = 70 years.

The age difference is constant at 70 − 63 = 7 years. Future ratio B : A = 15 : 14 has a difference of 1 unit.

Since 1 unit = 7 years, the future age of A = 14 × 7 = 98 years.

Required time x = 98 − 63 = 35 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of ages of A and B, 7 years ago = 8 : 9

Ratio of ages of A and B, 7 years after = 10 : 11

Age of B after x years = 15/14 of Age of A

**Formula Used:**

If present age is P, age t years ago is P − t, and age t years after is P + t.

 
•

 Total Difference = 14 Years

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the ages of A and B, 7 years ago, be 8k and 9k respectively.

⇒ Present age of A = 8k + 7

⇒ Present age of B = 9k + 7

⇒ Age of A after 7 years = 8k + 14

⇒ Age of B after 7 years = 9k + 14

⇒ According to the question, (8k + 14) / (9k + 14) = 10 / 11

⇒ 11 × (8k + 14) = 10 × (9k + 14)

⇒ 88k + 154 = 90k + 140

⇒ 90k − 88k = 154 − 140

⇒ 2k = 14 ⇒ k = 7

⇒ Present age of A = (8 × 7) + 7 = 63 years

⇒ Present age of B = (9 × 7) + 7 = 70 years

⇒ After x years, ratio of B to A = 15 : 14

⇒ (70 + x) / (63 + x) = 15 / 14

⇒ 14 × (70 + x) = 15 × (63 + x)

⇒ 980 + 14x = 945 + 15x

⇒ 15x − 14x = 980 − 945

⇒ x = 35

**∴ The correct answer is 35 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference in ages between any two individuals always remains constant regardless of the past or future years. This is the most crucial property used to simplify complex age problems.

Ratio Method for Ages

When the age ratio shifts symmetrically for both individuals over a given period, the difference in ratio units corresponds directly to the difference in years.

Linear Equations in Ages

If the present age is assumed as P, the age after t years will be P + t, and the age t years ago was P − t. Establishing these bases allows forming straightforward linear equations.
